{{Short description|American theoretical physicist}}
'''Martin B. Einhorn''' (14 August 1942) is an American theoretical physicist.<ref name=Kavli>{{cite web|title=Martin Einhorn|website=Kavli Institute for Theoretical Physics, U. of California, Santa Barbara|url=https://www.kitp.ucsb.edu/meinhorn}}</ref>

==Education and career==
Einhorn received in 1965 his B.S. with honors from Caltech and in 1968 his Ph.D. from Princeton University under Marvin Leonard Goldberger.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Physics Tree – Marvin Leonard Goldberger|url=https://academictree.org/physics/peopleinfo.php?pid=59148|access-date=2021-03-07|website=academictree.org}}</ref> After postdoctoral positions at [[Stanford Linear Accelerator Center]] (SLAC) and at the [[Lawrence Berkeley Laboratory]] (LBL), he became a staff physicist at the [[Fermi National Accelerator Laboratory]] (Fermilab). In 1976, he joined the faculty of the physics department of the [[University of Michigan]] where he was eventually promoted to full professor<ref name=Kavli/> and retired as professor emeritus in 2004.<ref>{{cite web|title=Martin B. Einhorn, Faculty History Project|website=lib.umich.edu, U. of Michigan|url=https://www.lib.umich.edu/faculty-history/faculty/martin-b-einhorn}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=INSPIRE|url=https://inspirehep.net/authors/1010908|access-date=2021-03-07|website=inspirehep.net}}</ref>

He was a visiting professor at [[NORDITA]], SLAC, the [[Hebrew University of Jerusalem]], the ''{{ill|Centre de physique des particules de Marseille|fr}}'' (CPPM), and [[Ben Gurion University of the Negev]] in [[Beersheva]].<ref name=Kavli/> In the 1990s he was on the [[Sakurai Prize]] selection committee.<ref name=DPF/>

{{blockquote|His research publications span topics in the [[Parton (particle physics)|parton model]], perturbative and nonperturbative [[Quantum chromodynamics|QCD]], cosmology, [[Higgs boson|Higgs physics]], supersymmetric grand unification, mass singularities and their consequences, and extended [[Technicolor (physics)|technicolor models]]. His primary interest is in physics beyond the [[Standard Model]].<ref name=DPF>{{cite web|title=DPF Newsletter – July 1, 1994 – American Physical Society, DPF Elections, Martin Einhorn, University of Michigan|website=aps.org (Division of Particles and Fields)|url=https://www.aps.org/units/dpf/newsletters/upload/july94.pdf}}</ref>}}

Einhorn is an emeritus research professor of [[University of California, Santa Barbara|UCSB's]] [[Kavli Institute for Theoretical Physics]] and was the Institute's Deputy Director from 1990 to 1992 and from 2004 to 2013.<ref name=Kavli/>

Einhorn worked as an Associate Director at University of California Stanford Linear Accelerator Center (SLAC) from 2011 to 2014.

==Honors and awards==
* 1978 — [[United States Department of Energy|Department of Energy]]'s Outstanding Junior Investigator Award
* 1991 — elected a Fellow of the [[American Physical Society]]
* 2003 — Guggenheim Fellowship<ref>{{cite web|title=Martin B. Einhorn|website=John Simon Guggenheim Memorial Foundation|url=http://www.gf.org/fellows/all-fellows/martin-b-einhorn/}}</ref>
